Astroray · lead session report · 29 Sep → 3 Oct 2026 · RTX 5070 Ti

Four nights and a long Saturday, 48 PRs, one much faster renderer

380 nm480580680780 nm

The GPU now renders the Cornell benchmark 2.85× faster than at the start of the week, and the sky noise that made Astroray look like confetti next to Cycles carries 75× less colour noise. Rebuilding the engine takes 8 minutes instead of 31. A real production node-tree corpus now exists, and the shader architecture to pass it is decided and landed. Stage 0 is not done, but it moved a lot on Saturday: marble passes all 16 channels on both backends (the first production material to do so), Light Path and Attribute nodes work on CPU and GPU, gate (d) is green, and gate (a) is scored with the worker staying off by default. Hair no longer lights itself, volume lights converge as 1/N, and the prism caustic now agrees with the referee to 1–3 %. The very last local build and test pass is deferred to next session, because you took the PC back; details in Housekeeping.

Speed: the GPU stopped tripping over itself

At the start of the week the GPU spent its time in two places: walking the BVH in software on a card with idle RT cores, and copying about 2 KB of path state onto the stack before every shading call. Both are fixed. Traversal moved to OptiX 9.1 on the RT cores (#1008), and the shade kernel was profiled with Nsight Compute and put on a register diet (#1014). Spectral upsampling had been scanning a 64-entry table linearly for every wavelength; it now bisects (#1013).

The profiling also produced the most useful sentence of the week: divergence is not the bottleneck; local memory is. 98.5 % of branches were uniform. The kernel was simply too big for its registers, and an earlier attempt to cap registers had capped a 40-register wrapper instead of the shader. That diagnosis is now in pkg300-shade-counter-attribution.md and will steer the next round.

Noise: from confetti to grain

Astroray picks one "hero" wavelength per path. Each pixel's handful of samples landed on random wavelengths, so flat skies came out as coloured confetti. pkg305 (#1003) stratifies the camera samples, the lens, the pixel filter and the hero wavelength together with a Sobol–Burley sequence, on CPU and GPU. No mean moved; only the noise did.

The new benchmark (pkg307) runs every corpus scene against Cycles CPU, Cycles OptiX and, for three spectral scenes, Mitsuba 3. It split the remaining gap into three causes: per-sample speed (now largely addressed), heavy tails in media and caustics, and no quasi-Monte-Carlo gain yet. The media tail had a single root cause, found overnight (next section).

Physics fixes: when two referees agree, believe them

The rule all week was physics first, then Mitsuba as an independent spectral referee, and Cycles only where Cycles is right. That rule found real bugs and also exonerated the engine twice.

Shader nodes: the long pole, now with a plan

You said complex shader node setups were the biggest practical hurdle, so the week opened by measuring it. pkg310 (#999) built eight realistic production materials with Cycles references and an audit for nodes that vanish without a warning. Baseline: 0 of 8 pass, and 39 "silent drops". Since then the textured Principled keeps all its layers (#1009), image textures tile (#1011), procedural textures evaluate per hit on the GPU instead of a blocky 64³ bake (#1023), and the silent-drop audit was rebuilt from the compiler itself so its 7 remaining drops are all real (#1028).

The architecture decision. Astra was asked whether to keep growing the small op-VM or move to a per-hit shader graph like Cycles' SVM. Verdict: a shared graph interpreter in its own GPU kernel, with the op-VM kept as a fast path and JIT later on the same IR. Bounds were never the real blocker; per-hit inputs and closure composition were. I adopted it (shader-graph-architecture-2026-10-03.md), and phases 1–2 landed that morning (#1030): old and new paths agree to 1e-6, wood went from 4/16 (CPU) and 3/16 (GPU) to 7/16 on both, and on a stress scene the graph programs take 0.511 s against the op-VM's 0.539 s.

Blender UI: native surfaces first

pkg311 phase 1 (#987) moved Astroray's own features onto Blender's own surfaces: a categorised Add menu, status lines on nodes that won't affect the render, a split Black Hole panel with units and presets (Sgr A*, M87*, Cyg X-1, with DOIs in the preset files), and sampling presets. No custom sidebar, as decided.

Build & tests: the bottleneck you named

You called build time the largest bottleneck. Splitting the 31-minute stage_advance.cu into twelve shade parts with identical kernels brought a fresh build to 8 minutes (#982), and it is what made a ten-lane night possible. The test suite went from 45 to 24 minutes, with a 7-minute fast profile (#979). Two quieter fixes matter as much:

  • A CUDA compile that failed with exit code −1 was reported as a success with a stale .pyd, because if errorlevel 1 never fires for negative codes. Fixed on main, with a backstop that fails any build log containing a ninja FAILED line.
  • My own merge watcher once merged a PR before CI had started, because "no checks yet" read as "no failures". Replaced with one that waits for real results; the one affected PR (#1013) needed a test-tolerance fix afterwards and is fine.

Afternoon and evening: eleven PRs that mostly landed

The last report ended with nine lanes still building. They finished. Each story below has the same shape: something looked fine, something was quietly wrong, a number proves it.

Hair was lighting itself (#1053, #1043)

A hair strand's hit point sits at the centre of the tube, so the next ray spawned from it started inside the strand and promptly hit it again. About 90 % of hair's indirect light was a strand talking to itself. The fix is Cycles' own trick, a self-primitive skip with no epsilon nudging, on CPU and GPU. Neighbouring segments of the same strand still count; only the one you left is skipped. Earlier that day the GPU's bare-scalp tuft turned out to be any instance in the scene making the GPU skip every curve (#1043), and the "GPU 11 % bright" bug (#853) was really the CPU's adaptive sampler giving up early.

Volume lights stopped tripping the tail (#1054)

Light-tree mode picked the anchor light at the middle of a ray segment, then picked again somewhere else. When the middle sat in the smoke and outside the spotlight's cone, there was no anchor and the fog never lit up. The fix ports Cycles' one pick per segment. GPU efficiency against Cycles OptiX on the media scene at 60 seconds went from 0.006 to 0.087, and the image's noise now falls as 1/N instead of getting stuck. Honest remainder: the shaft is still about 17× Cycles' variance per sample, from the smoke's global-majorant distance sampling (#1032).

Caustics: the GPU counted the same light twice (#1055)

Photon loops refracted deterministically, while the cull of path-traced lamp hits only caught strict enter/exit chains. Total-internal-reflection chains ended up in the photon map and in the path tracer. Both backends now use a Fresnel roulette and cull any receiver-to-caster-to-lamp chain; the CPU also builds a photon map from Blender at last. The arbitration scene was wrong too: its prism base sat exactly on the floor, so the "floor caustic" was really the prism. Lifted 5 mm, with a new Mitsuba reference and an independent numpy oracle that agrees to about 2 %. Corpus v2 prism floor GPU/CPU: 1.005.

CPU adaptive sampling was biased, and the reference was blessed on it (#1040)

The CPU stopped sampling pixels that had not yet met a rare light path, so hair read dark: ON/OFF luminance 0.882 before, 0.990 after (pooled seeds). The fix is Cycles' rounds of 16 with a 3×3 dilated mask. Stated residual: tile-edge pixels still read 0.970 against 0.9956 inside tiles. One CI reference, the refractive glass sphere, had been blessed on the biased engine; it was re-blessed on the fixed one.

Shader nodes: marble, the graph, Light Path (#1041, #1030, #1048)

Marble (#1041) is the first outright pass, 16/16 on both backends. #1030 landed the graph IR and a dedicated GPU kernel; #1048 added Light Path and Attribute / Color Attribute / Object Info. The corpus on main is 640 passed, 96 xfailed, 0 failed. Noise now matches Blender to 1.1e-4 at exact points, which is the number to quote when someone says "Noise looks off".

Decisions I made on your behalf

  • Shader architecture: adopted Astra's option B (shared graph interpreter). Easy to revisit before phase 3.
  • Codex: Sol 6.1 isn't offered to your account (only gpt-5.6-sol), so per your note hard thinking went to Astra. One Astra memo this run; reviews stayed on Terra.
  • Tolerances: pkg300's equivalence test uses 1e-5 × max(1, |ref|) because the old kernel varies by 1.3e-5 against itself on bright pixels; #1000's vertex delta path uses 4 float ULP. Neither loosens a physics gate.
  • Wood GPU 5/16 → 3/16 accepted for correct ring orientation over an aliased coincidence.
  • Adaptive sampling judged at equal work, not equal maximum samples.
  • Viewport worker default stays OFF (#1049): it wins five of six cells on p95. The ON path stays opt-in via ASTRORAY_VIEWPORT_WORKER=1.
  • Terra findings deferred to issues rather than blocking merges: #1045, #1046, #1047 (Light Path limitations) and #1050 (worker-OFF evidence needs retained present events).
  • Shadow-hop self fix done rather than disputed: #1053 first left Terra's last finding (transparent-shadow hops) as disputed; the merged state includes the fix.
  • Same-engine re-bless for #1040: the refractive-glass sphere reference had been blessed on the biased engine, so I re-blessed it on the fixed one instead of reverting a correct fix.
  • Removed the render-level melanin assertion (3a16065b): spectral-vs-RGB R/B differs by at most 0.4 % physically, against 0.3 % noise, so it could not detect a fallback and flaked on CI. #1056 adds a deterministic sigma_a(lambda) check that can (25–73 % apart from the RGB upsample at 400 and 700 nm).
  • The wall-clock test skipped on CI rather than loosened.
  • Out-of-gamut film values still clip at zero; whether scene-linear output keeps negatives (physically cleaner) is filed as #1024 for you.

Parked or failed

  • pkg300 full inlining hit a wall on the Principled call tree: forcing one function inline pushed others out of line. Phase 2 scene specialisation is the real fix.
  • CUDA 13 comparison: not run; only 12.6 and 12.8 are installed.
  • LuxCore and pbrt-v4 legs: downloaded, not wired into the benchmark.
  • Test-suite targets of 15 / 5 minutes: missed (24 / 7).
  • Open issues from today: #1051 (hair g/b/L still below Cycles), #1052, #1057.
  • Deferred Terra findings: #1045, #1046, #1047, #1050.
  • #1038 plain-Glass bias; #1032 smoke-VDB majorant sampling; #1034 object coordinates under motion blur.
  • Final local build, full suite, benchmark and showcase pass: deferred to next session (PC reclaimed).
  • Two usage-limit stops overnight; every lane resumed from its pushed branch with nothing lost.
